Hi Karthik / Marcus,

Following the onsite loop last week, the hiring team is recommending an offer for Andrew Tan (Sr. Backend Engineer, IC4-equivalent). Quick summary: strong systems design + shipping track record, will own ingestion surface for Redwood Optimize. Compensation needs to sit at the top of band to be competitive in SF.

Proposed package (draft):
- Base: $205,000
- Annual bonus: 15% target (discretionary)
- RSU grant: 18,000 RSUs v. 4 years, 1-year cliff
- One-time relocation stipend: $10,000 (exception request; candidate currently in Austin and has a short window to move)

I've attached the offer sheet and a short comp benchmark. Karthik — can you confirm this fits within the IC4 band when accounting for total cash and equity? Marcus — given the short timeline, can you weigh in on whether we should approve a one-time stipend outside the standard relocation policy?

If we have signoff by EOD I can send the offer and aim for a start date of 2024-09-02.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the packet. I reviewed the attached comp benchmark. Short answer: the proposed base + target bonus are at the 90th percentile for IC4 in SF. Total target cash (~$238k) plus the RSU package is slightly above our standard midpoint for IC4 but within the approved upper band for priority hires.

Notes:
- RSU sizing: 18,000 RSUs looks reasonable given market and candidate level; if we want to tighten cost we could 16k with a slightly higher cash mix, but candidate explicitly prefers equity.
- Bonus: 15% is fine; consistent with similar hires.

Relocation stipend: policy typically covers $5k for domestic moves under self-serve. A $10k one-time stipend is an exception but not unprecedented for highly constrained windows. From a comp budget perspective we can accommodate it as a one-time hiring exception (non-recurring).

Approve on comp grounds pending Marcus' ops/finance check.

—Karthik
